newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST - Taiwan April export orders seen sluggish.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Taiwan April export orders seen sluggish.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of local economists on Tuesday projected sluggish year-on-year growth of just 2.548 percent for Taiwan's April export orders, reflecting relative weakness in the second-quarter export season.
One key factor underlying the expected slow growth is the effect of an emergency March 20 ban on all pork exports due to an islandwide outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease.
The figures were due to be released by Taiwan's economics ministry at 0230 GMT on May 21.
Export orders in March rose 5.61 percent year-on-year.

"I don't see strong foreign demand emerging, so export performance in the second quarter should still be comparatively weak," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.

Economists said normal orders growth would be offset in part by the loss of an average US$130 million per month in foreign orders for Taiwan pork. Pork exports had been a US$1.56 billion a year business until the epidemic struck in March.
